A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe the same M3-VOS benchmark and ReVOS method. Their main text, eight-page supplements, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation evaluations, component ablations, annotation-quality studies, and object-size/velocity analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including ReVOS evaluations, ablations, and supplementary annotation and challenge analyses.

M1.justification: ReVOS retains the same reverse memory, mask booster, and readout fusion over frozen Cutie-base. The annotation tool and dual-model validation procedure are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same 479-video M3-VOS benchmark and full/core subsets, alongside VOST, DAVIS 2017, and YouTubeVOS-2019 evaluation. The five MEGA training datasets and represented phase-transition scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 4–5 retain DeAOT, XMem, RMem + DeAOT, SAM2, and Cutie-base as comparators. The newly cited InstaBoost and SRDA works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Metrics, Hungarian matching for Jcc, DAVIS-based checkpoint selection, DeAOT long-video exclusions, training schedule, and ablation settings remain unchanged. Supplementary annotation sampling and review procedures also match.

E4.justification: Both retain the same window/interval and component ablations in Tables 6–7, annotation-bias checks in Section 12, size/velocity analysis in Section 15, and failure cases in Section 16.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Existing reviewer averaging and randomized blind-comparison procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted or qualitative results match throughout, including the supplement. For example, Table 4 reports ReVOS J scores of 75.6 on M3-VOS full and 66.3 on core in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, phase and transition definitions, and the connected-component matching definition are retained. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a phase-transition benchmark, semi-automated annotation with dual-model validation, and plug-and-play bidirectional refinement through ReVOS.

C2.justification: The entropy-based motivation, scenery/phase-bias interpretation, annotation-bias limitations, small-object weakness, and failure-case explanations retain their meaning. Supplementary wording edits do not change these interpretations.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, hardware, training time, annotation instructions, and supplementary implementation details are unchanged. The existing project URL moves from the title block into the abstract; both versions still promise future code/data availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds InstaBoost and SRDA references and cites them alongside SAM2 in supplementary Section 12.1. This is a limited citation addition; the related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes local grammatical edits, especially in supplementary Sections 14–16, and adjusts paragraph breaks. Author contact text and Yong-Lu Li's name formatting change, while section order and nearly all prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The author block and page flow are reformatted, Figure 3 moves between columns, and supplementary failure-case panels are slightly resized. All figures and tables retain their scientific content.

improvement.justification: The added citations and light editorial/layout adjustments leave the scientific evidence, explanations, and reproducibility essentially unchanged. Existing issues also persist: Section 6.1 still calls SAM2 best on VOST despite Table 4 reporting J = 45.6 for DeAOT versus 44.1 for SAM2. The revision produces no meaningful net change in overall quality.
